subject: Control/Data plane service mapping + emergency rollback plan
body:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Devon Stahl <devon.stahl@cloudbridge.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 28 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Control/Data plane service mapping + emergency rollback plan

Devon — thanks again for the call this morning. As discussed, attaching the first-pass service mapping that shows where control-plane components (provisioning, auth, metadata) sit vs. data-plane inference nodes, and where CloudBridge will run the edge relay in their DC.

High level asks from our side:
- Confirm the relay-to-runtime TLS termination point (we expect CloudBridge relay will terminate mTLS to the onprem router and forward via TCP to the inference subnet).
- Confirm whether CloudBridge can host a standby relay in a separate AZ for failover (we'll need IP failover instructions).
- Read the rollback checklist and call out any steps that need your operational creds/assistance.

Attachments: service-map-v1.png, rollback-checklist.md

Planned next steps:
1) CloudBridge confirms TLS and standby relay plan by EOD Monday.
2) We iterate the service map and lock CIDR/port rules.
3) We run a controlled canary and verify KV cache warmup and prefetched weights behavior.

Kimberly — looping you for port/CIDR constraints and to call out anything we should pre-authorize on our firewall side.
Marissa — want to flag for the account and the go/no-go on the standby relay cost.

--
Jonas Weber
Sr. Program Manager, Deployments
Redwood Inference

-----Original Message-----
From: Devon Stahl <devon.stahl@cloudbridge.com>
Sent: Sat, 28 Nov 2026 09:45:12 -0800
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: solutions@cloudbridge.com
Subject: Re: Control/Data plane service mapping + emergency rollback plan

Jonas — thanks, received the map. Quick answers:
- Relay TLS: CloudBridge relay will terminate mTLS from the public-facing side and re-establish mutual TLS to the onprem router if you choose. Alternatively we can pass-through TLS if you prefer end-to-end encryption to the runtime nodes. The default we recommend (and what we sized for) is relay-terminate + relay->runtime mTLS.
- Standby relay: yes, we can run an active/passive standby in a separate AZ. We'll need a floating IP managed by your ops team or a VRRP handoff. We can support a scripted handoff if you prefer CloudBridge trigger.
- Rollback checklist: scanned, looks standard. We have two items to add: (a) a step to revoke relay certs if a compromised key is detected, (b) pre-staging of a read-only KV cache snapshot for faster rollback.

We'll get a short doc with the TLS modes and a suggested failover flow out by Monday noon.

—Devon
Devon Stahl
Principal Solutions Engineer
CloudBridge Inc.

On Sun, 29 Nov 2026 08:07:00 -0800, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com> wrote:

Jonas / Devon — a few technical clarifications from infra before we finalize the map:

1) Port requirements: we need exact destination ports on the inference nodes for both control-plane RPCs and data-plane streaming. Current defaults are 443 for mTLS, 9090 for internal control RPC, and 5555 for telemetry ingestion. Devon, can you confirm the relay preserves source IP if we ask? We rely on source IP in our telemetry egress rules.

2) CIDR isolation: the map shows a single /24 for runtime nodes; to support tenant isolation we would prefer splitting runtime into two /25s (tenant A/B) and tagging them in the ACL. That will affect the relay NAT rules.

3) KV cache warmup: for canary, we want cache pre-population for the first 5 tenants; if CloudBridge can accept a staged preload API call that would be ideal. If not, we'll handle it from our side but need time estimates.

4) Rollback sequencing: please confirm the order Devon recommended — revoke certs, cut traffic, mount read-only cache snapshot, rehydrate from snapshot where needed, and bring traffic back. Add me if we missed anything.

Attachments referenced: runbook-diff.pdf (two-line changes between our runbook and your standard CB-runbook).

Kimberly Park
Infrastructure Lead, Deployments
Redwood Inference

On Sun, 29 Nov 2026 11:15:39 -0800, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com> wrote:

All — quick commercial note: standby relay will add a small monthly charge from CloudBridge; if the customer (CloudBridge) is comfortable having active/passive managed by them it's cheaper. If Redwood wants CloudBridge to manage the floating IP and scripted failover we can approve the cost for pilot under CB-ENT-2026-0789. Confirm preference and I'll greenlight internally.

Also: please flag any security questionnaire evidence we need to supply for the standby relay (SOC2 evidence, cert stamping, drift monitoring).

Thanks,
Marissa
Director, Solutions & Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

On Sun, 29 Nov 2026 15:03:00 -0800, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com> wrote:

Thanks everyone — summary and decisions:
- Devon: please send the TLS modes doc + failover flow by Monday noon (we'll share in the Confluence page). Action: Devon (CloudBridge).
- Kimberly: we'll switch runtime CIDR to two /25s and publish a port matrix by EOD Monday. Action: Kimberly (Redwood).
- Marissa: please provision the pilot cost approval for CloudBridge-managed failover under CB-ENT-2026-0789 if we need CloudBridge to manage floating IP. Action: Marissa (Redwood).
- Operational ask: CloudBridge to confirm whether relay preserves source IP. If not preserved, we'll need to add X-Forwarded-For handling to the telemetry egress pipeline.

Attached final artifacts for this thread: service-map-v1.png (annotated), rollback-checklist.md (editable checklist), runbook-diff.pdf (differences). I've also uploaded them to Confluence: /display/INF/CB+Onprem+Integration+Notes (see related links).

I'll schedule a 30m follow-up Wednesday for validation and sign-off. If anything changes before then call me directly.

--
Jonas Weber
Sr. Program Manager, Deployments
Redwood Inference
